Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Goal: rapid FinOps-focused POC to validate performance and unit economics for a reranking + generation pipeline.
- Key asks: credit bands for staging vs. load tests, SLA floor for latency-sensitive routes, clear procurement path.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey thanks everyone for making time, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan Blake: jordan here, head of ML at Cobalt, hi all
[00:09] Maya Torres: maya, finance
[00:11] Priya Nair: priya, hello, doing SE things
[00:14] Sam Wu: sam, platform
[00:16] Lina Park: lina procurement
[00:18] Alex Chen: awesome, cool. Agenda — quick scoping on the poc: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and then the commercial guardrails — credits, pilot terms, and how we get to contracting.

[00:42] Jordan Blake: yeah we're excited. quick context: we run a two-stage flow — candidate generation on open model then rerank+response generation. Typical user sessions are small, 3 to 6 prompts, occasional long-form synthesis. Latency target for interactive flows is sub-500ms for the reranker and sub-1.2s for final gen at p50.

[01:05] Priya Nair: okay that's helpful — just to check, are those p50 or p95?
[01:09] Jordan Blake: those are p50 for the business case, p95 we want below 1.8s ideally.

[01:17] Maya Torres: from finance side wanting to see unit economics. our main metric is cost per successful session and success defined as above latency + quality threshold (nDCG improvement > 0.12 on our test set).

[01:37] Alex Chen: perfect — so success criteria: latency targets, cost per session, quality delta vs baseline. we'll include acceptance thresholds in SOW.

[01:50] Sam Wu: infra note — we plan to run the benchmark from our VPC, we can run agents from a staging cluster in our kubernetes environment, are there specific network requirements?
[01:59] Priya Nair: yes we support VPC peering for Redwood Private, and for hosted we'll set up egress rules. If you want on-prem we can also do the package but that usually takes longer.

[02:15] Jordan Blake: for this quick sprint we want hosted if possible, but with predictable cost so maybe dedicated or reserved burst?
[02:23] Diego Rivera: short answer: we can provision a small dedicated pool for the pilot (2 GPUs) for controlled throughput, and also set fallback to hosted variants. that lets you run deterministic benchmarks.

[02:40] Maya Torres: okay on credits — we prefer a clear credit cap and an overage policy. what's typical?
[02:47] Alex Chen: we usually do a three-tier credit band: dev/small bench, full benchmark sprint, and extended soak. For example: 5k credit dev, 50k for benchmark slices, 150k extended soak. credits map to token-equivalents and reserved capacity time.

[03:05] Maya Torres: and credits expire?
[03:07] Alex Chen: standard is 90 days, but for pilots we can do 120 days if procurement needs more runway.

[03:16] Lina Park: procurement needs a clear SOW and cost table to approve, and we prefer PO + net-30. who signs the SOW?
[03:23] Alex Chen: Redwood provides a simple SOW for the pilot with deliverables and acceptance criteria — typically signed by customer legal + Redwood legal. we'll include a sample.

[03:35] Jordan Blake: on benchmarking — we need to measure throughput (qps), latency p50/p95, token cost, and quality metrics. can Redwood run the tests or do we run them?
[03:45] Priya Nair: we can run with you or provide scripts. for impartiality, recommended to run jointly: customer drives traffic from your infra, Redwood captures serving telemetry and cost estimates.

[04:02] Sam Wu: question about KV cache and sequence lengths — our prompts average 90 tokens, but in some sessions up to 600 tokens for synths. will that change kernel selection?
[04:12] Diego Rivera: yes sequence distribution matters — runtime will pick different kernels and batching behavior changes. we'll need sample token histogram to tune quantization and batching.

[04:28] Jordan Blake: sending sample distribution is on our list. also want to try a 5k qps synthetic to test autoscale but only if needed. for the POC we'll probably aim for 500 qps baseline.

[04:42] Alex Chen: noted — so bench plan: 1) functional correctness + quality runs (small), 2) latency profile at 500 qps, 3) stress to 5k if we agree, 4) extended soak for 24-72 hours.

[05:00] Maya Torres: another financial question: credits to dollars mapping, and if we move to Dedicated how does that change billing?
[05:07] Alex Chen: dedicated shifts to reserved capacity pricing — monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go credits. SOW will show both modeled: per-token run-rate vs reserved GPU hour model. we'll model your 3-month runway.

[05:22] Jordan Blake: any minimums?
[05:24] Alex Chen: pilot minimums are flexible; we normally ask for a small reserved pool for deterministic results, but we can do hosted credits only if procurement prefers zero infra commit.

[05:36] Maya Torres: need to see sample cost modeling spreadsheet.
[05:39] Alex Chen: yeah we'll attach a cost model (spreadsheet) with breakouts: token cost, caching savings, batching delta, infra commit delta.

[05:51] Lina Park: timeline question — procurement lead time for a pilot PO is typically 2-3 weeks. is that doable?
[05:58] Alex Chen: yes — if we get SOW and PO templates early we can turn around. ideal sequence: agree scope this week, Redwood sends SOW/credit proposal by Fri 8/8, Cobalt signs PO by week of 8/18, kickoff bench week of 8/25.

[06:15] Priya Nair: security notes — you mentioned audit logs and KMS?
[06:19] Sam Wu: yes SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves, and we use GCP KMS currently.
[06:25] Priya Nair: Redwood supports SOC2, SSO (SAML/OIDC), audit logs, and KMS integrations — for hosted we have customer-controlled KMS via key wrapping; for Private we can hand off full key ownership. we'll attach the security pack.

[06:42] Jordan Blake: great. also want to ensure PII redaction on logs for benchmark runs.
[06:46] Diego Rivera: we have configurable redaction and field-level masking in the pipeline; we'll include the config snippet in the security pack.

[06:56] Maya Torres: is there a standard SLA for dedicated pilot?
[06:59] Alex Chen: pilot SLAs are advisory — for pilots we commit to operational support and a high-availability baseline; formal SLA is part of Dedicated enterprise contracts. but we can agree to response time targets in the SOW.

[07:13] Jordan Blake: on acceptance criteria for quality — we'll provide an eval set and threshold like nDCG > 0.12 improvement and F1 > 0.6 for classification tasks.

[07:24] Priya Nair: we'll instrument the eval harness to capture those. also flagging potential model variant fallbacks — we can route to a cheaper quantized model if the heavy model is throttled. that's part of cost controls.

[07:39] Sam Wu: how much instrumentation do we need to add on our side?
[07:43] Priya Nair: for the bench we need request IDs and token counts per request; ideally a header with user-session id and route name. minimal changes.

[07:55] Jordan Blake: okay good, we'll add that.

[08:00] Alex Chen: quick note on the credit mapping — we estimate cost per session at current baseline, and show delta with Redwood; that will be in the spreadsheet.

[08:10] Maya Torres: if we exceed credits, do you automatically cut us off?
[08:13] Alex Chen: no automated cut off — we'll alert and pause if requested; overages invoiced monthly unless you prefer a hard cap.

[08:22] Lina Park: procurement wants sample contract language for PO + SOW — non-negotiable items?
[08:28] Alex Chen: standard is mutual confidentiality, limited liability, and IP carveouts for your customer data. we can send redlines.

[08:38] Jordan Blake: competitor note — we're evaluating Anthropic for rerank, but they lack the dedicated routing we're after. also doing some open-source runs but costs spike.

[08:50] Priya Nair: good to call out — Redwood Optimize recommendations will show batching/quantization suggestions to reduce token spend.

[09:00] Sam Wu: one more thing — do you provide dashboards per-route during the POC?
[09:04] Diego Rivera: yes console access with per-route latency/cost, traces, and sample logs; retention during pilot is 30 days unless otherwise agreed.

[09:17] Jordan Blake: excellent.
[09:20] Alex Chen: ok i'm going to recap next steps and responsibilities — Jordan, you'll share the sample prompts, traffic CSV, and eval set; Maya and Lina will help with procurement timeline and PO template; Redwood will send the SOW, credit tiers, cost model, and the security pack. We'll also schedule the benchmark kickoff.

[09:42] Maya Torres: timeline looks fine; procurement will push for net-30 and PO.
[09:46] Lina Park: yep will try to expedite.
[09:48] Alex Chen: any other open Qs?
[09:50] Jordan Blake: none from me, thanks everyone.
[09:53] Priya Nair: thanks all — we'll wait for the files.
[09:55] Alex Chen: great, we'll follow up via email. bye.
